Summary  
Data source overview: The excerpt is the reference list and extended-data descriptions from the 2015 Nature paper “Human-level control through deep reinforcement learning” (DQN).  Although presented mainly as citations, the text still states—via the figure captions, tables, and surrounding discussion—the key causal story: classical RL algorithms were unstable and data-hungry; DeepMind combined experience replay, a separate target network and a deep CNN encoder to stabilise and speed up learning from raw pixels; empirical tables and visualisations show the resulting performance and representation quality.

Inference strategy justification:  The paper explicitly gives methods (experience replay, target network, CNN encoder) and validation (Extended Data Tables/Figures).  The top-level safety-relevant risks (instability, sample inefficiency, poor generalisation) are implicit; they are standard problems the methods are meant to solve and are directly mentioned in the Supplementary Discussion.  Moderate inference (edge confidence 2) was used only where the text implies, but does not spell out, the causal link (e.g. representing “policy-invariant features improve generalisation”).

Extraction completeness explanation:  Three distinct risk threads were extracted and joined through the shared “Unified DQN architecture” node, giving one connected knowledge fabric that covers all interventions discussed (experience replay, target network, CNN encoder, mixed human/agent replay, full DQN).  Framework decomposition requirement is met by breaking DQN into its internal mechanisms instead of using one monolithic node.

Key limitations:  
1. The data source is mainly references; fine-grained details of some mechanisms (e.g. specific hyper-parameters) are not present, so deep implementation nodes rely on standard DQN descriptions.  
2. Generalisation risk is only lightly supported by Figure 1; confidence is therefore lower (edge confidence 2).  
3. Interventions are evaluated only on Atari games, limiting external validity.
